title: SerialDash protocol v1 — device to app
description: Validates the JSON payload of a device→app protocol line, i.e. everything after the leading `@`. A line whose `t` is not one of these is a message type unknown to this protocol version: the app is required to ignore it rather than reject it, so it is intentionally outside this schema's `oneOf` (new message types can be introduced without breaking old apps).

channelValue.description: The shapes a channel's value can take in a `d` message. This uses `anyOf` rather than `oneOf` on purpose: e.g. a 2-number array is simultaneously a valid [x, y] pair and a valid array of numbers — which one it means depends on which widget is consuming it, not on the JSON shape itself.

hi.description: Sent once by the device right after it starts (and again any time the app asks for one by sending its own `hi`). Identifies the device and its protocol version, and is normally followed immediately by the device's `w` widget declarations.

v.description: Protocol version the device speaks. The app uses this to know which message shapes to expect.

name.description: Device name shown in the app's status bar and About panel.

fw.description: Firmware version string, shown alongside the device name. Entirely up to the sketch — not interpreted by the app.

board.description: Board name, e.g. "ESP32" or "Uno". Optional and purely informational.

rx.description: Size, in bytes, of the device's incoming line buffer. Tells the app how long an app→device line is safe to send before the device would have to truncate or drop it.

w.description: Declares one widget on the dashboard. The exact set of allowed properties depends on `k`, the widget kind.

u.description: Updates an existing widget's properties in place, without redeclaring it — only the given fields change, everything else about the widget stays as it was. `id` and `k` can't be changed this way; to change a widget's kind, remove it (`x`) and declare it again.

x.description: Removes a widget from the dashboard, or every widget this device has declared if `id` is omitted.

d.description: Carries one or more channels' current values. The most frequent message type on the wire — sent every time the device has new sensor/state data to report.
Map of channel id to its new value. A channel doesn't need its own widget — an undeclared channel can still auto-create one, depending on the app's settings.

ts.description: Device-side timestamp (typically `millis()`), in milliseconds. Lets the app align samples from a device that buffers or batches data instead of always using arrival time. Omit if the device has no clock worth reporting — the app then just timestamps the data on arrival.

e.description: A log event — shown in the app's console and in any `log` widgets. Used for status messages, warnings, and errors the device wants to surface, as distinct from regular channel data.

src.description: Optional origin label (e.g. a subsystem name), usable to filter a `log` widget to just this source.

ack.description: The device's response to an app→device `c` control command, matched back to it by `r`. Every `c` gets exactly one `ack` — the app's UI depends on it to know whether the command succeeded.

r.description: Echoes the `r` of the `c` message this acknowledges.

ok.description: Whether the command was accepted. When `true`, the device is expected to also send a `d` with the control's actual resulting state.

err.description: Human-readable reason the command was rejected. Only meaningful when `ok` is `false`; shown to the user in the app.

pong.description: The device's response to an app→device `ping`, matched back to it by `r`. The app uses the round trip to show connection latency and to detect a device that's stopped responding.

r.description: Echoes the `r` of the `ping` message this answers.
